title: Solana Stories: Stablecoin Adoption is not Fake
description:
Ahmed Zifzaf, Head of Crypto Partnerships at Worldpay, grew up watching the Egyptian pound fall from 3:1 to 50:1 against the dollar. That experience sent him to Argentina, Nigeria, Brazil, Colombia, and Thailand to see whether      stablecoin adoption was real.                             

Ahmed shares what he saw on the ground, and why Worldpay chose Solana to build their stablecoin settlement product.
                                         
DISCLAIMER
The content herein is provided for educational, informational, and entertainment purposes only, and does not constitute an offer to sell or a solicitation of an offer to buy any securities, options, futures, or other derivatives related to securities in any jurisdiction, nor should not be relied upon as advice to buy, sell or hold any of the foregoing. This content is intended to be general in nature and is not specific to you, the user or anyone else. You should not make any decision, financial, investment, trading or otherwise, based on any of the information presented without undertaking independent due diligence and consultation with a professional advisor.  Solana Foundation Foundation and its agents, advisors, council members, officers and employees (the “Foundation Parties”) make no representation or warranties, expressed or implied, as to the accuracy of the information herein and expressly disclaims any and all liability that may be based on such information or any errors or omissions therein. The Foundation Parties shall have no liability whatsoever, under contract, tort, trust or otherwise, to any person arising from or related to the content or any use of the information contained herein by you or any of your representatives. All opinions expressed herein are the speakers’ own personal opinions and do not reflect the opinions of any entities.

asr.full_text: As an Egyptian-American who grew up in Dubai, I got exposed to a lot of very unique economies. When I was seven, it was $1 to 3 Egyptian pounds. Today it's 50 Egyptian pounds to $1. A currency being devalued starts to affect you even at that age. You literally see purchasing power evaporate. How can you improve financial systems so that they work for everyone When I first started at worldpay I went and lived in Argentina, Nigeria, Brazil, Colombia, Thailand I wanted to know are people actually using stable coin The adoption is not fake Sehri has two banks left You go to Lebanon, and their currency has completely devalued to the point where it's artwork In Argentina, some restaurants don't have fixed menus because every week they have to raise their prices. Your purchasing power has just completely been annihilated. Everyone should have the opportunity to improve their livelihood. Which blockchain are we using to do a blockchain payments product? And when you look at Solana, they're so open about how they're operating and how their technology works and going to policy makers to get in front of them, to get them comfortable, as a highly licensed companies. Those are all things that make us very confident, really excited to be able to take the latest innovations Stablecoin settlement on Solana make sure that when people think of payments they don't think of it as a cost center they think of it as a value out, you don't have to deal with Debit Rails and Credit Rails Sepa and Swift and Pix with Stablecoin you log and CEPA and SWIFT and PICS. With Staples, you log into your app and send money to any address around the world, and I think the more that we can give access to that, the more that it makes a lot more sense to use the internet to do all of our financial transactions as we already do. In my role at WorldPay, I also get to do humanitarian payment work. Afghani refugees receive two billion dollars in cash from the U.S. Those come in armored planes that cost something like $50 million a year to send. Is there another way to develop trust? Is there another way to develop transparency? When you think about crypto, it can save people in many unfortunate situations, and you can proliferate that safety net to everyone if you do it the right way.
